regime_context: Hong Kong’s eligible-theme roster has narrowed to five names (Tech Hardware, Conglomerates, Banks, Industrials, High-Dividend Blue Chips). The absolute-trend gate is the only validated edge, and it currently permits exposure to these five. The two scorable themes (China Tech & Internet and China Platform Megacaps) both fail the gate, so the gate’s drawdown-avoidance signal suggests caution on them.

theses.subject: China Tech & Internet
theses.thesis: The absolute-trend gate, which is the detector’s single validated risk-control leg, marks China Tech as eligible=false. Given gate_helps is true for this market, an ineligible theme has historically been associated with higher drawdown risk; thus a lean to avoid is consistent with the gate’s discipline (not a return forecast).
evidence: gate_helps = true (backtest: gate materially reduces volatility/drawdown when applied)
low durability (0.38) and trend-following signal are insufficient to override the gate
theses.dissent: A sudden policy/catalyst (e.g., major China internet stimulus or AI news) could cause sharp mean-reversion in beaten-down tech names, making trend-based risk controls look overly conservative.

falsifier.text: The absolute-trend gate flips China Tech & Internet to eligible=true before the 20-day check-by date.

theses.subject: Tech Hardware & Semis
theses.thesis: Tech Hardware is the headline narrative, passes the absolute-trend gate (eligible=true), shows trend-like behaviour (hurst_tag=trend, durability 0.57), is not crowded, and the gate is a validated drawdown-avoidance mechanism. An overweight lean is defensible as a lower-risk trending theme, not as a return forecast.
theses.dissent: Extremely low breadth (0.167) means the theme is driven by a handful of stocks; a sharp reversal in any heavyweight could break the trend violently, and the absolute-trend gate does not prevent single-name blow-ups.

falsifier.text: The absolute-trend gate flips Tech Hardware & Semis to eligible=false before the 20-day check-by date.
